**Settings used throughout.** `reference_kappa` and `reference_mu0` define the reference prior (explained in the model section). `physical_limit` is the speed above which a codon is treated as physically implausible.

```{r}
reference_kappa <- 0.5
reference_mu0 <- 0.5
physical_limit <- 50   # codons/s

setting_name <- function(kappa, mu0) paste0("κ = ", kappa, ", μ₀ = ", mu0)
reference_setting <- setting_name(reference_kappa, reference_mu0)
```

# Data (To change)

```{r}
codon_count <- readxl::read_excel("data_files/Codon_counts.xlsx")[c(1:6600),] %>% column_to_rownames("...1")

codon_freq <- codon_count %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric))/rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Gene")

TE <- readxl::read_excel("data_files/Total_unified_TE_extrapolation.xlsx")
```

**Keeping only the 61 sense codons, and converting ES to codons/s**

```{r}
codon_freq <- codon_freq %>% select(-c(TAG,TGA,TAA))
TE <- TE %>% mutate(total_unified_ES = (total_unified_TE*CDSLength)/(3600*3*MeanNumberOfRibosomes))
```

```{r}
extrapolated_tot <- TE %>% drop_na(total_unified_ES) %>%
  mutate(CDS_bins_400 = cut(CDSLength,breaks=c(min(CDSLength),
                                               400,
                                               800,
                                               1200,
                                               1800,
                                               max(CDSLength)),
                            include.lowest = TRUE))
```

**One table per bin.** The response `inv_ES` is $1/ES$ in seconds per codon. Stop codons were included when the frequencies were calculated, so each gene's 61 frequencies sum to slightly less than one. Dividing by the row sum makes them sum to exactly one, so that the model's weighted sum is a true average.

```{r}
make_dwell_data <- function(bin_label) {
  bin_table <- extrapolated_tot %>%
    filter(CDS_bins_400 == bin_label) %>%
    select(SystematicName,total_unified_ES)
  bin_table <- merge(bin_table,codon_freq, by.x = "SystematicName", by.y= "Gene")
  bin_table <- bin_table %>% column_to_rownames("SystematicName")
  f <- bin_table[, -1]
  f <- f/rowSums(f)
  out <- data.frame(inv_ES = 1/bin_table$total_unified_ES, f)
  rownames(out) <- rownames(bin_table)
  out
}

dwell_data <- list(II = make_dwell_data("(400,800]"),
                   III = make_dwell_data("(800,1.2e+03]"),
                   IV = make_dwell_data("(1.2e+03,1.8e+03]"))

bin_labels <- c(II = "400-800 nt", III = "800-1200 nt", IV = "1200-1800 nt")
bins <- names(bin_labels)
codons <- sort(colnames(dwell_data$II)[-1])

bin_pairs <- tribble(
  ~Pair,                        ~Bin_1, ~Bin_2,
  "400-800 vs 800-1200 nt",     "II",   "III",
  "400-800 vs 1200-1800 nt",    "II",   "IV",
  "800-1200 vs 1200-1800 nt",   "III",  "IV") %>%
  mutate(Pair = factor(Pair, levels = Pair))

observed_level <- imap_dfr(dwell_data, ~ tibble(Bin = .y,
                                                Bin_label = factor(bin_labels[[.y]], levels = bin_labels),
                                                genes = nrow(.x),
                                                median_inv_ES = median(.x$inv_ES),
                                                median_ES = 1/median(.x$inv_ES)))
observed_level
```

**Genes lacking a codon.** `missing_codons` counts the genes in which at least one of the 61 sense codons is absent. A log-ratio transform of the codon frequencies would need a replacement value for each of these zeros.

```{r}
missing_codons <- imap_dfr(dwell_data, ~ tibble(Bin = .y,
                                                Bin_label = factor(bin_labels[[.y]], levels = bin_labels),
                                                genes = nrow(.x),
                                                genes_lacking_a_codon = sum(rowSums(.x[, -1] == 0) > 0),
                                                share = mean(rowSums(.x[, -1] == 0) > 0),
                                                median_codons_absent = median(rowSums(.x[, -1] == 0))))
missing_codons
```

# The dwell-time model

A ribosome spends an average of $\tau_c$ seconds on codon $c$, its *dwell time*. The time to translate a gene is the sum of the dwell times of its codons, so the time per codon of gene $g$ is the frequency-weighted average of the dwell times:

$$\frac{1}{ES_g} = \sum_c f_{gc}\,\tau_c$$

The speed of a codon is $v_c = 1/\tau_c$ in codons/s, and the speed of a gene is the harmonic mean of its codon speeds. The model has no intercept, because a gene made of a single codon would have $1/ES = \tau_c$. The frequencies act as weights in an average, which is the explicit treatment of the compositional constraint that the reviewer asks for.

The full model has three levels:

$$\log\frac{1}{ES_g} \sim \text{Normal}\Big(\log\sum_c f_{gc}\tau_c,\ \sigma\Big)$$

$$\tau_c \sim \text{Gamma}\big(\text{mean} = \mu,\ \text{CV} = 1/\sqrt{\kappa}\big)$$

$$\mu \sim \text{LogNormal}(\log \mu_0,\ 1), \qquad \sigma \sim \text{Exponential}(1)$$

-   **Gene-level noise.** Genes differ for reasons other than codon composition. Each gene's time per codon is its mechanistic value multiplied by a random factor, with spread $\sigma$ on the log scale. $\sum_c f_{gc}\tau_c$ is then the *median* of $1/ES_g$, so the model describes a typical gene.
-   **Shared average.** All codons share a mean dwell time $\mu$, which is estimated from the data. A codon with little information is pulled towards the average codon and not towards a number chosen in advance.
-   **Spread between codons.** $\kappa$ sets how far codons may differ from $\mu$: their coefficient of variation is $1/\sqrt{\kappa}$. It is fixed, and the section "Why the spread between codons is fixed" shows why.

## Stan program

The program below is written directly in Stan, because `brms` cannot estimate the mean of a prior on regression coefficients. `F` is the gene x codon frequency matrix and `y` is $1/ES$. In Stan, `gamma(a, b)` has mean $a/b$ and CV $1/\sqrt a$, so `gamma(kappa, kappa / mu)` has mean $\mu$ and CV $1/\sqrt\kappa$. `F * tau` gives $\sum_c f_{gc}\tau_c$ for every gene at once.

```{r}
dwell_stan_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;                  // number of genes
  int<lower=1> K;                  // number of codons (61)
  matrix<lower=0>[N, K] F;         // codon frequencies, each row sums to 1
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;            // 1/ES = mean dwell time per codon of each gene (s)
  real mu_loc;                     // prior on mu: centre on the log scale
  real<lower=0> mu_scale;          // prior on mu: spread on the log scale
  real<lower=0> kappa;             // fixed concentration of the dwell times around mu
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu;                // average codon dwell time (s)
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;          // codon-specific dwell times (s)
  real<lower=0> sigma;             // spread of the gene-level noise on the log scale
}
model {
  mu ~ lognormal(mu_loc, mu_scale);
  tau ~ gamma(kappa, kappa / mu);          // mean mu, coefficient of variation 1/sqrt(kappa)
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  y ~ lognormal(log(F * tau), sigma);      // median = sum_c f_gc * tau_c
}
"

dwell_model <- cmdstan_model(write_stan_file(dwell_stan_code, dir = "fits", basename = "dwell_time_shared_mean_lognormal"))
```

## Prior settings

The settings vary the two things that are chosen by hand. $\kappa$ ranges from a CV of 200% ($\kappa$ = 0.25) to 25% ($\kappa$ = 16). At the reference $\kappa$, the centre of the prior on $\mu$ moves two-fold in either direction.

```{r}
dwell_settings <- bind_rows(
  tibble(kappa = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 4, 16), mu_centre = 0.5),
  tibble(kappa = reference_kappa, mu_centre = c(0.25, 1))) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(kappa, mu_centre) %>%
  mutate(Setting = setting_name(kappa, mu_centre),
         Setting = factor(Setting, levels = Setting),
         mu_scale = 1,
         tau_cv = 1/sqrt(kappa),
         Reference = Setting == reference_setting)
dwell_settings

setting_colours <- setNames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2")[seq_len(nrow(dwell_settings))], levels(dwell_settings$Setting))
```

## Fitting

`fit_dwell()` runs the model on one bin: 4 chains with 2000 warm-up and 2000 sampling iterations, giving 8000 posterior draws. It keeps the draws of `tau`, `mu` and `sigma` and the convergence diagnostics, and saves them in `fits/`. Later sections call it without a file and with fewer iterations.

```{r}
fit_dwell <- function(data, kappa, mu_centre, mu_scale = 1, file = NULL, iter = 2000, seed = 2025) {
  if (!is.null(file) && file.exists(file)) return(readRDS(file))
  F <- as.matrix(data[, -1])
  fit <- dwell_model$sample(
    data = list(N = nrow(F), K = ncol(F), F = F, y = data$inv_ES,
                mu_loc = log(mu_centre), mu_scale = mu_scale, kappa = kappa),
    chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = iter, iter_sampling = iter,
    seed = seed, refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE)
  tau <- fit$draws("tau", format = "matrix")
  out <- list(tau = matrix(as.numeric(tau), nrow = nrow(tau), dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(F))),
              mu = as.numeric(fit$draws("mu", format = "matrix")),
              sigma = as.numeric(fit$draws("sigma", format = "matrix")),
              diagnostics = tibble(max_Rhat = max(fit$summary(c("mu", "tau", "sigma"), "rhat")$rhat),
                                   min_ESS_bulk = min(fit$summary(c("mu", "tau", "sigma"), "ess_bulk")$ess_bulk),
                                   divergences = sum(fit$diagnostic_summary(quiet = TRUE)$num_divergent)))
  if (!is.null(file)) saveRDS(out, file)
  out
}

dwell_fits <- expand_grid(dwell_settings, Bin = bins) %>%
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(kappa, mu_centre, mu_scale, Bin), function(k, m, s, b) {
    fit_dwell(dwell_data[[b]], k, m, s,
              file = file.path("fits", paste0("dwell_lognormal_", b, "_kappa_", k, "_mu0_", m, ".rds")))
  }))

pick_fit <- function(setting, bin) dwell_fits$fit[[which(dwell_fits$Setting == setting & dwell_fits$Bin == bin)]]
```

## Convergence

$\hat R$ compares the variation within and between chains and should be below 1.01. `min_ESS_bulk` is the smallest effective number of independent draws over all parameters, and a few hundred or more is fine. Divergent transitions mark regions the sampler could not explore and should be 0.

```{r}
convergence <- dwell_fits %>%
  mutate(diag = map(fit, "diagnostics")) %>%
  select(Setting, Bin, diag) %>%
  unnest(diag)
convergence
```

## Codon summaries

Each row of `codon_post` is one codon in one bin under one setting. Speeds are the inverse of dwell times, so the lower end of a speed interval comes from the upper end of the dwell-time interval. Rank 1 is the fastest codon.

```{r}
summarise_codons <- function(tau) {
  tibble(Codon = colnames(tau),
         Tau_median = apply(tau, 2, median),
         Tau_low = apply(tau, 2, quantile, 0.025),
         Tau_high = apply(tau, 2, quantile, 0.975),
         Tau_sd = apply(tau, 2, sd)) %>%
    mutate(Speed = 1/Tau_median,
           Speed_low = 1/Tau_high,
           Speed_high = 1/Tau_low)
}

codon_post <- dwell_fits %>%
  mutate(summ = map(fit, ~ summarise_codons(.x$tau))) %>%
  select(Setting, kappa, mu_centre, Bin, summ) %>%
  unnest(summ) %>%
  group_by(Setting, Bin) %>%
  mutate(Rank = rank(Tau_median)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Bin_label = factor(unname(bin_labels[Bin]), levels = bin_labels))

reference_post <- codon_post %>% filter(Setting == reference_setting)

reference_wide <- reference_post %>%
  select(Bin, Codon, Speed) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Bin, values_from = Speed)
```

```{r}
data_out <- reference_post %>%
  transmute(Codon, Range = as.character(Bin_label), Speed, Speed_low, Speed_high, Dwell_time = Tau_median, Rank) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Range, values_from = c(Speed, Speed_low, Speed_high, Dwell_time, Rank), names_glue = "{.value} ({Range})")

data_out_key <- tibble(Column = c("Speed", "Speed_low", "Speed_high", "Dwell_time", "Rank"),
                      Description = c("Posterior median of 1/tau (codons/s)",
                                      "Lower limit of the 95% credible interval of 1/tau",
                                      "Upper limit of the 95% credible interval of 1/tau",
                                      "Posterior median of tau (s per codon)",
                                      "Rank of the codon by posterior median speed (1 = fastest)"))

writexl::write_xlsx(list(`Codon level speeds` = data_out, key = data_out_key), "Codon_Speed.xlsx")
```
